newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks seen rising in technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks seen rising in technical rebound.

text.p: South Korean stocks are expected to rise in a technical rebound on Friday following the past four consecutive days of declines, brokers said.
But they said the overall mood would be fragile on concerns about corporate financial troubles and the Hansol Group saga.
They predicted the index would be supported by an expected rebound of blue chips in response to their recent sharp drops.
"Cautiousness will continue to prevail due to persistent negative factors," said Kim Ik-hwan of Hyundai Securities.
The composite index ended down 4.41 points at 684.69 on Thursday.
Renewed concerns about corporate financial troubles were sparked by Tuesday's application by a textile maker for court receivership after it defaulted on its debt payments.
Trading in Yu Sung Co shares resumes on Friday after a two-day suspension. Brokers saw Yu Sung, now put under the supervision list, falling sharply.

The Hansol Group, which a newspaper report said had managed a fund on behalf of an associate of President Kim Young-sam's son, will continue to draw attention. Most of the seven listed Hansol units fell early on Thursday but recovered to end flat.
